Comments: This is a follow-up inspection of the clean-up of a release of produced fluids to ground observed during an inspection on 10/30/2024. Clean-up of contaminated soil was completed on 12/30/24. Operator, Jack Cochran, stated he would return to the site when weather permitted to remove the water with a vac truck, restore the site with clean material, remove tanks, and repair and complete the deck on the bridge. This work has not been completed, previously cited violations remain open on this permit. The depression left from the clean-up needs to be backfilled with clean fill material, a second layer of boards need to be put down and side rails attached to complete the bridge deck and fill added on the either side of the bridge.Violations to be lifted when clean-up is completed and bridge repair completed. Manifest and tipping receipts for disposal of contaminated soil and water required by the Department before violations can be lifted.This clean-up of a brine/oil release and bridge repair has been in process for over a year and needs to be completed.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Penneco Oil Co Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-11-13
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 867976
Permit API: 125-22730
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-11-13
Comments: On 11/13/19 a follow up inspection of the site was conducted in response to violations noted on 7/14/16 and in preparation for a meeting with the operator. The following was observed: >>The initial inspection found: "The access road that leads to NAT Industries 1&2 leads through a section of wetland. The tire tracks were submerged in roughly 6-12” of water at the time of inspection and were surrounded by wetland vegetation including cattails and duckweed. This constitutes a violation of 25 Pa. Code § 105.11(a) for failing to obtain a permit from the Department prior to constructing, modifying, or maintaining a water obstruction or encroachment." >>A follow up inspection on 8/15/19 found: "The access road to the site was expanded and reinforced with the wetland area remaining present on either side. This continues to constitute a violation of 25 Pa. Code § 105.11(a) and 35 P.S. § 691.402(b) in that site features were constructed within the Waters of the Commonwealth without a permit." >>On 11/13/19 the site was found to be unchanged from the 8/15/19 inspection with the violations ongoing. No new violations were found. A meeting with the operator is scheduled for 11/14/19 to discuss appropriate remediation plans and permits for the site.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 5/12/2025 at 1:48 pm, Tonya Winkler notified the Department that there was a 20 gallon spill from secondary containment due to a tear in the liner.On 5/13/2025 at 11:15 am, I completed an incident inspection. The spill was cleaned up at this time. The liner was temporarily repaired with tape and a valve was replaced.Mark Veltri sent me a text on 5/13/2025 at 1:07 pm that included pictures of the cleanup. NGE took field readings following the removal of impacted material and pulled 5 confirmation samples for the lab.INR intends to replace the taped secondary containment area with a more robust containment and a felt liner underneath to help prevent punctures. Please send the Department the final clean up report and waste manifest for the impacted material.Violations were cited for the release from secondary containment. The violations were immediately corrected and closed.

Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for broken and corroded piping and a release from broken and corroded piping.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4106039, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department attempted to contact the Operator by calling the number posted on the well tag, however, the number was not in service, therefore violations are being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate information posted on the well posting.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank under/adjacent to the corroded pipes. Although, these soil conductivity readings (0.0328 mS, 0.0899 mS, and 0.0244 mS) are not elevated, it does not visual appear that the release that previously occurred has yet to be remediated as vegetation in this area appears to be distressed and the gravel in this area is stained. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping is to remain outstanding at this time and new violations are being issued at this time for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/23/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8235149
Permit API: 015-23440
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 985708
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/21/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator concerning the discovery of fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) in the north central area of Pad B. It rained heavily while I was traveling up the access road and it stopped before I reached Pad B. Along the access road, a sediment discharge into UNT 18 to Frozen Run was observed. Sediment-laden fluid was observed flowing from the access road, underneath a section of silt fence, overtop of a line of compost filter sock, and entering the stream. It was noted in inspection report number 3505502 from 2/13/23 that the potential for a sediment discharge continued to exist in this location due to stormwater from the access road overtopping a line of compost filter sock. The Department recommends adding additional compost filter sock to prevent additional sediment discharges into the stream. Violations remain outstanding for the sediment discharge into the UNT 18 to Frozen Run along the access road. These violations remain outstanding against the ESCGP.On Pad B, the pad was covered with puddles of stormwater due to the recent precipitation. In the northcentral area of the pad, an excavated section approximately 60 feet by 10 feet is present along the pad edge where the pad meets the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid in this area was between 17.18 mS/cm and greater than 19.99 mS/cm. A sump is installed in the pad surface to the south of the north stormwater channel. Fluid is present in the sump approximately 2 feet down and an EC reading could not be obtained at this depth. The fluid in the north stormwater channel in the north central area had an EC of 11.97 mS/cm. The fluid flowing out of the northeast end of the north stormwater channel and into the lined sump has an EC ranging between 16.14 mS/cm and 19.18 mS/cm. The fluid within the lined sump at the end of the channel had an EC of 18.05 mS/cm. It appears that all of the fluid flowing out of the stormwater channel at the surface is being collected by the lined sump. No fluid was observed surrounding the sump. EC readings of the soil surrounding the sump were all below 200 uS/cm. In the northwest area of the pad surface where the dancefloor had been located, the stormwater had an EC of approximately 1600 uS/cm or less. The EC of fluid in the stormwater channel at the northwest corner of the pad was approximately 1400 uS/cm. Northwest of the MASS the fluid on the pad surface had an EC of 2.48 mS/cm. In the northeast corner of the pad surface, the EC of the fluid was 5.26 mS/cm. The fluid east of the MASS had an EC of 2.39 mS/cm. The fluid within the secondary containment southeast of the MASS was approximately 8 mS/cm. Fluid near the southeast corner of the pad, where elevated EC fluid was found by the Department on 2/6/23, had an EC of 2.80 to 4.68 mS/cm. The Department recommends screening the entire pad surface for elevated electrical conductivity and vacuuming up any fluid found with elevated electrical conductivity.Violations noted for the fluid discovered in the northcentral area of the pad surface. Due to the unknown volume and origin of this fluid, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8156115
Permit API: 121-44463
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/21/2023
Comments: Onsite for a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3602052 dated 8/17/2023. The previous inspection report references a black plastic brine line, (2) brine tanks, and a separate tank battery with (4) steel tanks.There is a 100bbl fiberglass tank and a 100bbl poly tank onsite that appears to be the brine storage tanks for the well. The two tanks are plumbed together with piping and valves open to equalize the fluid in each tank. There does not appear to be a way to empty either tank by means of a water truck hose connection without altering the plumbing of the tanks. However, the 2" black poly line that runs from the hillside from the wells on the lease and ties into the brine tanks has a "T" fitting and a valve to discharge produced fluid to the ground via a ditch from a cross-culvert of the access road.The 2" valve on the black poly pipeline is closed and plugged. The pipe was not actively discharging or leaking. However, there is a visible impact area within the ditch of the cross-culvert and which the black poly line is laid. Soil conductivity readings indicate that a brine discharge has occurred at the site. The impacted area inside the ditch extends approximately 80' downslope from the access road culvert and ending just before a second culvert for another old access road. The width on average of the ditch is about 5'. The amount of the discharged produced fluid is unknown.Violations are cited.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: 78a55(i)5vi - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Planning - Failure of the unconventional well operator to have a copy of the emergency response plan at the well site during all phases of operation.
Violation ID: 8268984
Permit API: 125-23384
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Hopewell Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On March 25, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 11H OG Well located on the Cowden 15 well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. Accompanying during today's inspection is DEP WQS Tyler Metzger and Big Dog Energy (BDE) representative Mr. Scott. BDE is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 15 well pad, however, according to DEP records, Diversified owns both the well pad and the gas wells on this well pad. To date, the DEP is unaware of a pending transfer of ownership from Diversified to BDE. During IR 4139773, violations were issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance, all information that is required to be posted on the Act 9 sign appears to be BDE's. Both on-site mailboxes that are attached to the Act 9 sign were observed to be empty at the time of this inspection. Mr. Scott stated that they are still waiting to receive the ERP back from the company who they hired to make it and that at this time he does not have a timeline as for when it will be received and available on site. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to have the ERP on site. The Department requests the Operator provide the Department with a schedule of when the ERP will be available on site by COB 4/8/2026.At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any wells on the Cowden 15 well site are in production yet (the 11H, 12H, and 15H). Mr. Scott stated that they are waiting for equipment to arrive (anticipating an arrival by the end of the week) and once it does they intend to be in production. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the 11H gas well to be surrounded by cement barriers and had a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this gas well. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a separator, 2 GPUs, and 3 green production tanks within secondary containment, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment. A white above ground storage tank was also observed to be on site, however it did not appear to be connected to any other production equipment at this time. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. Based on today's inspection, violations issued to the 11H gas well for a lack of an Emergency Response Plan on site is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On 1/7/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 40 degrees and overcast when I arrived on site. Snow and ice from recent snowfall events still covered the facility.During the inspection, Moody and associates had a team on site collecting samples from the three clean-out standpipes from the monitoring trenches draining from the well cellars. A conductivity reading from the east clean-out pipe was 1.14 mS conductance. There are four active wells on site staged for production, along with one plugged well and one that is in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H well has a monument with plugged date of 12/4/2024. The 5H well still has the production valve attached. The production tanks and GPUs are staged in secondary containment.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed below the excavated/remediated areas. Ice and snow cover the restored area. Temporary stabilization could be seen in areas not covered by snow. PCSM structures have not been installed at this location.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 3999274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance.I left the site at 1400 hours.

Comments: On 7/15/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4187078, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. At the time of this inspection, no formal NOV Response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. Since the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. Since the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.On 4/02/2026, Big Dog Energy representative responded via email to IR 4168852 and stated "As the DEP is aware this well was sold to Murphy Production in 2024. However in regards to the spill there was none. I ordered a new sign to put up just so this well can be transferred along with an ERP plan. Should have it within a week to install and get transferred to Murphy" (IR 4174382). However, the well site was unchanged at the time of the following inspection conducted on 4/27/2026 (IR 4187078). The following was observed during the inspection:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 12). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 7, 8, 10, and 11). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photos 1-3). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photo 6). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team. The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 4 and 5). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photos 1, 9, and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4187078 remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no formal NOV Response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

The pad surface has been covered with rock and appears very stable, and rock for maintaining the pad surface and access has been stockpiled on the pad. Violation ID: 8191187
Permit API: 129-26032
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/14/2024
Comments: On June 14, 2024 the Department conducted a Routine Inspection of the Joseph A Negri 1 well located in East Huntington Township, Westmoreland County. During a previous inspection (IR 3723492) the Department observed a drum on site with a Methanol label on it. At that time the Department requested the operator provide information by 3/29/24 on what exactly is in the drum and what it is being used for, the Department also requested that the Operator remove all equipment not necessary for production. The Department has not received a response from the Operator in regards to this site.At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. A well tag with all required information posted on it was fixed to the wellhead. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. Some production equipment onsite that appeared to be in production due to the gauge attached to it had an open pipe close to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the well site in some vegetation as a background (0.0074 mS) and then a reading was taken directly next to the piping (0.409 mS) and then a little further back from this piping (0.382 mS). The production tank also had some wet marks coming from the top of the tank and the wet marks can be seen going down the tank towards the ground in areas. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the production tank below areas where the wet marks were observed on the tank (0.1483 mS and 0.1405 mS). The drum of methanol was observed to still be on site, not in secondary containment and fluid can be seen sitting at the top of it with air bubbles forming from what may be a small hole or crack in the top of the barrel. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the drum (0.096 mS), as well as in the fluid sitting at the top of the drum (0.620 mS).The soil conductivity readings taken near the open pipe and at the base of the production tank are elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading and subjugate that there is some sort of release contaminating the soil in both areas. The reading at the base of the Methanol drum is comparable to the background, but the fluid sitting at the top and the air bubbles seen indicate that there may be a leak at the top of the drum which currently has the potential to reach the ground. While onsite, the Department spoke with Dave Lindahl of Mountain View to let him know about the elevated readings by the production equipment and production tank and informed him about the possible hole at the top of the Methanol Drum. The Department recommended the drum be removed or put in secondary containment as soon as possible and recommended they determine how the two leaks occurred, stop them, remove all contaminated soil, replace it with new top soil, and seed/mulch. Dave stated that someone would be onsite on 6/17/24 to begin working on all of this. The Department is recommending the Operator either remove this drum or put it within secondary containment by COB June 28, 2024. Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not currently in use and for a release from production equipment.

Comments: This administrative inspection documents the receipt of sample results for samples taken on the pad on 4/17/19 and samples taken in the sediment ditch (background and where fluid from the pad entered) and sediment trap outfall taken on 4/18/19. The sample from the pad (ID #0939078) shows elevated levels of barium and strontium, and while the chloride result was cancelled, these elevated parameters show that the high conductance fluid on the pad was likely a release produced water or flowback. The elevated chlorides, barium, and strontium in sample ID #0939080 (as compared to background, represented by sample ID #0939079) show that the fluid migrated from the pad, into the ditch, and into the sediment trap. Sample ID #0939081 taken from the sediment trap outfall shows higher levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides than the sediment ditch background sample, demonstrating that the fluid was released from the sediment trap. The failure to report a release of a regulated substance to the ground is a violation of 25 PA Code 78a.66(b). The release of the fluid to the pad surface is a violation of 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and the Solid Waste Management Act (35 PS 6018.301). The release of the fluid to the ditch, sediment trap, and outfall is a violation of the Clean Streams Law (35 PS 691.401). Due to the unknown volume and duration of this release, this site will be required to go through the Act 2 process.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/09/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Seneca Resource's Hepler D 235 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 1/9/2023 at 1030 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of diesel fuel reported by Seneca Resources. Complaint tracking system (CTS) identification # 369178 is tied to this release within CTS. A diesel powered glycol heater had a pinhole leak in a fuel line that caused diesel fuel to release to an interior secondary containment which also had a leak, releasing diesel fuel to a secondary containment structure beneath the entire unit. The secondary containment structure on the ground was discovered to be leaking, which released a mixture of diesel fuel and stormwater to the ground surface. While onsite, company personnel evaluated the impacted area and determined the release to be estimated at 35 gallons of diesel fuel mixed with stormwater from the containment. Crew began by recovering all of the diesel on the surface with a portable vacuum unit. The glycol heater was then transferred to a new, functional secondary containment outside of the impacted area. Once a residual waste container arrived onsite, excavation of the impacted area began. A Seneca representative stated later that 1.5 to 2 inches of pad material was scraped from the impacted area. All impacted material was placed into a lined residual waste container for later disposal. Excavation and remedial activities were completed by 1300 hours on 1/9/2023. The glycol heater unit was repaired and it's secondary containment was replaced. No portion of the diesel fuel release was able to escape the pad surface.Based on the findings of this inspection report, the reported release made by Seneca Resources, and the timely remediation completed by the operator, violations of the following are cited against API #117-21531 as immediately corrected:25 Pa. The secondary containment structure on the ground was discovered to be leaking, which released a mixture of diesel fuel and stormwater to the ground surface. While onsite, company personnel evaluated the impacted area and determined the release to be estimated at 35 gallons of diesel fuel mixed with stormwater from the containment. Crew began by recovering all of the diesel on the surface with a portable vacuum unit. The glycol heater was then transferred to a new, functional secondary containment outside of the impacted area. Once a residual waste container arrived onsite, excavation of the impacted area began. A Seneca representative stated later that 1.5 to 2 inches of pad material was scraped from the impacted area. All impacted material was placed into a lined residual waste container for later disposal. Excavation and remedial activities were completed by 1300 hours on 1/9/2023. The glycol heater unit was repaired and it's secondary containment was replaced. No portion of the diesel fuel release was able to escape the pad surface.Based on the findings of this inspection report, the reported release made by Seneca Resources, and the timely remediation completed by the operator, violations of the following are cited against API #117-21531 as immediately corrected:25 Pa.
